security_audit.summary: The skill intentionally runs local PowerShell and Python commands for SharePoint auditing. Several markdown backtick findings are false positives, but the installer and audit commands are real external-command risks. No prompt injection or malicious exfiltration intent was found in SKILL.md.

content.value_statement: SharePoint permission reviews can be slow and inconsistent across sites. This skill guides a local audit workflow that collects inputs, runs approved tools, and locates reports.
actual_capabilities: Collects tenant ID, app ID, PFX path, internal domains, and site scope.
Checks that PowerShell, Python, and PnP.PowerShell are available locally.
Runs the local PowerShell module installer for the audit workflow.
Runs the local Python audit agent for one site or a CSV-defined batch.
Points users to generated HTML reports and warns about sensitive contents.
limitations: Requires local PowerShell 7.4+, Python 3.10+, and PnP.PowerShell.
Requires certificate authentication and a PFX_PASS environment variable.
Uses local shell commands and may install PowerShell modules.
Audits permissions only; it does not automatically fix access issues.

use_cases.title: Review One Site
use_cases.description: Audit permissions for a single SharePoint Online site and locate the generated HTML report.

use_cases.title: Audit a Site Batch
use_cases.description: Run the same permission review across sites listed in a CSV file.

use_cases.title: Prepare Compliance Evidence
use_cases.description: Generate permission reports that support internal reviews and access governance checks.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Single-Site Audit
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for one SharePoint site.
prompt_templates.prompt: Guide me through a local SharePoint permissions audit for one site. Ask for each required input before running commands.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Sites from CSV
prompt_templates.scenario: Batch audit using a site list.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me run a SharePoint permissions audit for sites in a CSV file. Confirm my local prerequisites and output location.

prompt_templates.title: Check Sensitive Handling
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my audit inputs for safe handling. Confirm that secrets will stay out of chat, logs, and generated reports.

prompt_templates.title: Assess Report Results
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review after an audit run.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the generated SharePoint audit report to summarize risky permission patterns and note items that need human review.

output: The skill asks for tenant ID, app ID, PFX path, internal domains, and site URL.
It confirms local tool versions and the PFX_PASS environment variable.
It points to the generated HTML report and warns that it contains sensitive data.
The skill confirms the CSV input and output folder.
It runs the local audit workflow for the listed sites.
It identifies where each site report is stored.
The skill keeps Read as the default Sites.Selected scope.
It asks for explicit authorization before using Write permission.
It reminds the user to use the least privilege needed.

best_practices: Confirm local tool versions and tenant details before starting the audit.
Use read-only Sites.Selected permissions unless Write is clearly authorized.
Protect certificate secrets and generated reports as sensitive data.
anti_patterns: Running audit commands before reviewing tenant, app, and site inputs.
Pasting PFX_PASS into chat, command output, or shared logs.
Granting Write scope for an audit that only needs read access.

faq.question: What does this skill audit?
faq.answer: It audits SharePoint Online permissions for one site or a CSV-defined site batch.

faq.question: Does it require local tools?
faq.answer: Yes. It expects PowerShell 7.4+, Python 3.10+, and PnP.PowerShell on the operator machine.

faq.question: How does it authenticate?
faq.answer: It uses certificate authentication with a PFX path and the PFX_PASS environment variable.

faq.question: Does it change SharePoint permissions?
faq.answer: No. It is designed for auditing and report generation, not automatic permission remediation.

faq.question: Are reports sensitive?
faq.answer: Yes. Generated reports can contain permission details and should be stored with access controls.

faq.question: Can it run in Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
